prompt:
Write article.css for long-form case studies on our site. The markup is `<article class="prose" lang="en">` with p, h2, h3, em, abbr (acronyms such as WCAG, SAP and API, sometimes inside an em passage), a small results table of numbers and an uppercase eyebrow label `.eyebrow`. Body text is Source Serif 4, self-hosted: fonts/SourceSerif4[opsz,wght].ttf with fonts/SourceSerif4-Italic[opsz,wght].ttf beside it. Headings, the eyebrow and the results table use Outfit: fonts/Outfit[wght].ttf. Read the font files, do not modify them. Use the fonts' OpenType features where they genuinely help. Save article.css and a short notes.md explaining the font decisions.

Input files: fonts/SourceSerif4[opsz,wght].ttf, fonts/SourceSerif4-Italic[opsz,wght].ttf, fonts/Outfit[wght].ttf
assertions: notes.md states the features consistently with the files: Source Serif 4 roman has onum, smcp, c2sc and case; Source Serif 4 italic has onum and case but no smcp or c2sc; Outfit has tnum but no onum, smcp, c2sc or case
article.css sets the Source Serif 4 body paragraphs in oldstyle figures (oldstyle-nums or "onum")
article.css sets abbr acronyms in the Source Serif 4 roman body in true small caps (all-small-caps, or c2sc plus smcp) with positive letter-spacing

Acronyms inside em passages cannot be rendered as synthesized small caps: font-synthesis (or font-synthesis-small-caps) is none for them, or article.css resets them to normal capitals, and notes.md or a comment says the italic has no small caps

article.css requests no oldstyle figures, small caps or case-sensitive forms (no oldstyle-nums, onum, small-caps, all-small-caps, smcp, c2sc or "case") for Outfit text, unless a comment beside the rule says the font lacks the feature and the rule is inert
article.css sets the results table numbers in Outfit with tabular-nums and gives the uppercase .eyebrow positive letter-spacing
article.css declares the Source Serif 4 roman and italic files and the Outfit file in @font-face with weight ranges, the italic with font-style: italic, and disables font-synthesis for the text
Rendered at a 1280px-wide viewport with Source Serif 4 and English sample prose, full body lines in .prose average between 58 and 74 characters
